## Explore the very best of British art

Tate Britain is free to visit. Our new collection displays explore 500 years of British art and its many stories and voices. Discover much-loved favourites alongside new contemporary artworks, from the Pre-Raphaelites to [David Hockney](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/david-hockney-1293), [Bridget Riley](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/bridget-riley-1845) and [Lubaina Himid](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/lubaina-himid-cbe-ra-2356). Tate Britain is also home to the world’s largest collection of works by [JMW Turner](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/joseph-mallord-william-turner-558).

Entry to the gallery is free – there’s no need to book. Booking a ticket is recommended for [exhibitions](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?date_range=from_now&event_type=exhibition&gallery_group=tate-britain) but some tickets may be available at the door. [Members](https://shop.tate.org.uk/membership) enjoy unlimited free entry to exhibitions with no need to book.

## Admission information

### Entry details

Entry to the [collection](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?date_range=from_now&event_type=display&gallery_group=tate-britain) is free for everyone. Booking is recommended for [exhibitions](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?date_range=from_now&event_type=exhibition&gallery_group=tate-britain).

#### Exhibition entry

- Members and Supporters enjoy free exhibition entry – no need to book, just turn up with your card
- Visitors with a disability pay a concessionary rate, and entrance for companions is free
- Visitors aged 16–25 can join Tate Collective to access £5 exhibition tickets
- Up to four children aged 11 and under go free per parent or guardian
- £5 family child tickets are available for children aged 12–18 years

For more information see our [Booking and Ticketing FAQs](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/frequently-asked-questions/ticketing).

#### Entrance

The Millbank entrance will be closed until 2027 for the construction of the Clore Garden. Please use the Manton Entrance on Atterbury Street.

#### Bag size policy

Bags are checked on arrival so please allow extra time for security checks.

We reserve the right not to allow any bag, parcel, or other item to be brought into the gallery.

Potentially dangerous objects are also not permitted.

Bags and items larger than cabin bag size (55cm x 40cm x 20cm) are not permitted in the building. Potentially dangerous objects are also not permitted.

Wheely luggage and cabin bags are not permitted in ticketed exhibitions.

There is a left luggage facility at [Victoria station](https://www.nationalrail.co.uk/stations/VIC/details.html).

#### Skateboards, scooters, and folding bike policy

Electric skateboards, scooters and folding bikes are not permitted in the building. Non-electric skateboards, scooters and folding bikes are permitted but must be stored in the cloakroom. Cloakroom capacity is limited, so we regret that at busy times we may not be able to accept these items.

#### Security

We take security very seriously and work closely with [Police Project Servator teams](https://www.met.police.uk/projectservator). You can read more about our approach to [safety and rules for the gallery](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-gallery-rules).

### Opening times

Monday to Sunday 10.00–18.00

Last entry 17.30, galleries start closing 17.50

### Accessible car parking

There are five accessible parking spaces for disabled visitors, accessed via John Islip Street. Please book these spaces at least 24 hours in advance.

#### To book accessible parking:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 - option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00) 

 Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps

_Your name, contact details, vehicle registration number, date and time of visit are required to make the booking for an accessible parking space_.

Once you have parked, please enter the Gallery via the Manton Entrance, approximately 200 meters from the parking spaces. If you have booked a mobility scooter or wheelchair, these can be collected from the Staff Entrance.

#### Drop off points

There is a drop off/pick up point on Atterbury Street and one on Millbank. These are both near the entrance to the gallery.

#### Parking spaces for Blue Badge holders

There are three spaces for Blue Badge holders on Atterbury Street, by a dropped kerb and three spaces on Millbank.

### Entrance

The Millbank entrance will be closed until 2027 for the construction of the Clore Garden. Please use the Manton Entrance on Atterbury Street.

- There is a ramp down to the Manton entrance with central handrails.
- The Manton entrance has automatic sliding doors.
- The Manton entrance takes you to the lower floor of the gallery where there is level access to the Linbury Galleries, the Hyman Kreitman Reading Rooms by appointment only, Café, toilets and baby care room.
- There is lift and stair access to the gallery areas on the main floor.

### Wheelchair and mobility scooter provision

To borrow a wheelchair or walker you can either book in advance or ask a member of staff on arrival (subject to availability). Reservation is free.

To borrow a mobility scooter please book at least 24 hours in advance of visiting. Reservation is free but you must have driven a mobility scooter before.

#### To book:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 - option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)

Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps

_Your name, contact details, date and time of visit are required to make the booking_

### Facilities at Tate Britain

#### Toilets

Accessible and standard toilets, along with baby changing facilities are located on the Lower Floor.

A [Changing Places](http://www.changing-places.org/) toilet is also located on the Lower Floor, which offers:

- Plenty of room for carers
- Electric hoist equipment (please bring your own sling suitable for a loop system)
- Height adjustable changing bench
- Paper roll
- Height adjustable wash hand basin
- Non-slip floor
- Privacy screen

You can access the toilet using a RADAR key, which you collect from the staff reception on John Islip Street. The John Islip Street staff entrance has level access and is available if you have booked accessible parking.

If you are already in the gallery or have not entered via John Islip Street, a member of staff can guide you to the facilities.

#### Lifts

- A large lift near the Manton Entrance gives access up to the gallery areas on the main floor. The lift is to the left of the ticket desk, opposite the Manton Studio.
- A large lift near the Lower Rotunda, near the [Djanogly Café](https://visee.tate.org.uk/tate-britain/visiting-information/eat-drink/djanogly-cafe), gives access up to the gallery areas on the main floor and the [Members Room](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/members-room) on the upper floor.
- Floor levels are announced in all lifts.

#### Seating

- There are seats and benches near the Manton Entrance and Lower Rotunda.
- There are also a number of seats in the galleries.
- Folding seats are available – just ask a member of staff or pick up a stool from the racks located in the galleries.

#### Water fountains

Water fountains are located next to the toilets on the lower floor. There is also a water dispenser in the Djanogly Café.

#### Cafe

The [Djanogly Café](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/djanogly-cafe) is located on the lower floor with access from the Lower Rotunda.

#### Shops

There are two shops at Tate Britain:

- The [Main Shop](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/main-shop) is on the upper floor and accessible as part of the free collection routes.
- The [Manton Shop](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/manton-shop) on the lower floor is located in the Manton foyer and is accessible to all visitors twice during their visit.

#### Member Facilities

The [Members Room](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/members-room) is located on the upper floor. Access the Members Room via the lift located at the Lower Rotunda on the lower floor, near the Djanogly Café.

#### Multi-Faith and Contemplation Room

A multi-faith and contemplation room is available on the main floor in the [JMW Turner](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/display/jmw-turner) galleries - ask a member of staff for location. This is a designated space for worship and prayer, as well as quiet and reflection. All are welcome to use this room.

#### Quiet Room

A quiet room is available to use on the main floor, adjacent to the [Play Studio](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-britain/edward-burra/play-studio-dream-worlds). This room is for neurodiverse people, families or anyone who would like to spend some quiet time away from the gallery environment.

### Assistance dogs

We welcome guide dogs, hearing dogs and assistance dogs in the gallery. Drinking bowls are available from a member of staff at the cloakroom in the Manton foyer.

### Autism

To help plan your visit to Tate Britain, have a look at our [visual story](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/tate-britain-visual-story-1). It includes photographs and information of what you can expect from a visit to the gallery.

When you get to the gallery, ear defenders can be borrowed. Please ask a member of staff.

The Clore foyer tends to be the quietest place in the gallery. Ask a member of staff for more information.

Loud noises, flashing lights, smoke effects and strobe lighting feature in some artworks.

A quiet room is available to use on the main floor, adjacent to the Play Studio. This room is for neurodiverse people, families or anyone who would like to spend some quiet time away from the gallery environment.

For more information before your visit contact us on:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call [+44 (0)20 7887 8888](tel:+44(0)2078878888) - option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)

_Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps_

### Blind and visually impaired visitors

#### Enlarged print gallery plans

Enlarged print gallery plans are available on request.

#### Large print guides

Large print guides are available for all exhibitions.

You can access printed versions in the gallery:

- Ask a member of staff the exhibition entrance.

You can access PDF versions on our website:

- Visit the relevant exhibition page and click on the blue box 'Read the exhibition guide'; click on the 'Download large print guide' button near the top of the page to read the guide or to save a copy to your device.

Large print captions are currently not available for the permanent collection. Visitors can borrow a magnifier from one of the Information Desks.

#### Magnifiers and Coloured Overlays

Magnifiers and coloured overlays are available from exhibition entrances. Ask a member of the gallery team for more information.

#### Audio description: _Ways of Looking at Art_

You can listen to a [spoken description of our _Ways of Looking at Art_ film](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-britain/ways-of-looking-at-art#audio-description).

### Deaf and hard of hearing visitors

#### Hearing loops

The following areas of Tate Britain are fitted with a hearing loop:

- Auditorium
- Manton Studio

### Dyslexic visitors

Large print guides, coloured overlays and magnifiers are available for exhibitions. Ask a member of staff at the exhibition entrance.

### Epilepsy and Seizures

Loud noises, flashing lights, smoke effects and strobe lighting feature in some artworks.

For more information before your visit contact us on:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)

### Communication cards

Communication cards provide a means of visual, or nonverbal, communication.

You can use our communication cards to ask for directions to facilities in the gallery. These include toilet, café, seating, shop, quiet room, and exit. Show one of the cards to a member of Tate staff if you need to be shown to one of these places.

You can download these cards and print at home or save as a PDF on your portable device. There are two colour versions, with white or yellow background. Use whichever version you find easiest to read.

- [Print at home communication cards (white) 36.22 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1716/communication_cards_white_print.pdf)
- [Print at home communication cards (yellow) 35.96 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1717/communication_cards_yellow_print.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (white) 36.65 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1718/communication_cards_white_digital_1.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (yellow) 39.41 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1719/communication_cards_yellow_digital.pdf)

_Tate is grateful to Anna Farley who initiated and championed the development of these communication cards. Anna is an autistic artist who makes work exploring her autism, UK disability culture and inclusion._

## Explore modern and contemporary art from around the world

See some of the world’s most exciting modern and contemporary art at Tate Modern. Enjoy innovative works that have shaped art as we know it. Our gallery is free to visit. On display are paintings, sculptures and large-scale installations from artists around the world including [Pablo Picasso](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/pablo-picasso-1767), [Yayoi Kusama](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/yayoi-kusama-8094) and [Henri Matisse](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/henri-matisse-1593). Explore the iconic Turbine Hall alongside our underground Tanks, a striking space dedicated to live performances and video.

Members enjoy unlimited free entry to exhibitions with no need to book.

## Admission information

### Entry details

Entry to the collection is free for everyone. Booking is recommended for exhibitions.

#### Exhibition entry

- [Members](https://shop.tate.org.uk/membership) and Supporters enjoy free exhibition entry – no need to book, just turn up with your card
- Visitors with a disability pay a concessionary rate, and entrance for companions is free
- Visitors aged 16–25 can join [Tate Collective](https://www.tate.org.uk/tate-collective) to access £5 exhibition tickets
- Up to four children aged 11 and under go free per parent or guardian
- £5 family child tickets are available for children aged 12–18 years

For more information see our [Booking and Ticketing FAQs](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/frequently-asked-questions/ticketing).

#### Entrance

Entry is via the Turbine Hall ramp or via the Blavatnik Building.

#### Bag policy

Bags are checked on arrival so please allow extra time for security checks.

We reserve the right not to allow any bag, parcel, or other item to be brought into the gallery.

Potentially dangerous objects are also not permitted.

Bags and items larger than cabin bag size (55cm x 40cm x 20cm) are not permitted in the building.

Wheely luggage and cabin bags are not permitted in ticketed exhibitions.

There is a left luggage facility available at London Bridge stations.

#### Storing your personal items

Lockers are available to rent on L0 of the Blavatnik Building. The lockers do not accept cash.

Dimensions and prices:

- Standard (£4, 36cm x 30cm x 43cm)
- Large (£6, 44cm x 36cm x 42cm)
- Jumbo (£8, 58cm x 44cm x 66cm)

Lockers are free of charge for Tate Members.

Please note that the cloakroom in the Natalie Bell Building on Level 0 has now closed.

#### Skateboards, scooters, and folding bike policy

Electric skateboards, scooters and folding bikes are not permitted in the building, nor are the batteries removed from these e-vehicles. Non-electric skateboards, scooters and folding bikes are permitted, but must be stored in the cloakroom at Tate Britain or in the paid locker facilities at Tate Modern (lockers are free of charge for Tate Members). Please note that cloakroom and locker capacity is limited, and during busy periods we may not be able to accept these items. We advise you check the dimensions of your items in advance to ensure they fit within our locker size limits.

#### Security

We take security very seriously and work closely with [Police Project Servator teams](https://www.met.police.uk/projectservator). You can read more about our approach to [safety and rules for the gallery](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-gallery-rules).

### Opening times

Sunday to Thursday 10.00–18.00

Friday to Saturday 10.00–21.00

Last entry 30 minutes before closing time

### Accessible car parking

There are twelve parking spaces for disabled visitors, accessed via Park Street. Please book these spaces at least 24 hours in advance.

#### To book accessible parking:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 – option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)
- Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps

_Your name, contact details, vehicle registration number, date and time of visit are required to make the booking for an accessible parking space_

Once you have parked, enter via the South Entrance of the Blavatnik Building across the level terrace, approximately 30 – 60 metres from the parking spaces. 

Two RADAR Key operated lifts link the South Entrance on Level 1 and the Ticket desks in the Turbine Hall. RADAR keys are available from staff at the South Entrance on Level 1 and ticket desks on Level 0.

If you have booked a mobility scooter or wheelchair, these can also be collected from the South Entrance.

### Entrance

Entrance is via the Turbine Hall or via the Blavatnik Building from Park Street.

### Wheelchair and mobility scooter provision

To borrow a wheelchair or walker you can either book in advance or ask a member of staff on arrival (subject to availability). Reservation is free.

To borrow a mobility scooter please book at least 24 hours in advance of visiting. Reservation is free but you must have driven a mobility scooter before.

#### To book:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 – option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00) 

 Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition app

_Your name, contact details, date and time of visit are required to make the booking_

### Facilities at Tate Modern

#### Toilets

Fully accessible toilets are located on every floor on the concourses.

A [Changing Places](http://www.changing-places.org/) toilet is available on Level 0 of the Natalie Bell Building.

You can access the toilet using a RADAR key. RADAR keys are available from the tickets desk on Level 0 and from staff at the South entrance on Level 1.

It offers:

- Plenty of room for carers
- Full room coverage electric hoist equipment
- Height adjustable changing bench
- Paper roll
- Height adjustable wash hand basin
- Non-slip floor
- Privacy screen
- Seating

#### Baby changing facilities

- The Baby Care Room is located on Level 0 Natalie Bell Building
- Additional nappy-changing facilities are available in toilets on levels 0 to 5

#### Lifts

- There are four lifts in the Natalie Bell Building, by the main stairs on each floor. You can reach the lifts from the Turbine Hall. These lifts are being prioritised for people who are not able to use the stairs or escalators
- There are eight lifts in the Blavatnik Building, situated by the main stairs on each floor
- Two RADAR Key operated lifts link the South Entrance on Level 1 and the Ticket desks in the Turbine Hall on Level 0. RADAR keys are available from staff at the South Entrance on Level 1, and from the cloakroom and ticket desks on Level 0

#### Seating

- There are seats and benches throughout the gallery.
- Folding seats are available – just ask a member of staff or pick up a stool from the racks located on the concourses on levels 2, 3 and 4

#### Water fountains

Water Fountains are located next to the toilets in the Natalie Bell building on Levels 1, 2, 3 and 4

There is also a water dispenser in the [Espresso Bar](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/natalie-bell-building-espresso-bar) in the Natalie Bell building on Level 3

#### Food and Drink

There are opportunities to buy food and drink at Tate Modern:

- The [Espresso Ba](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/natalie-bell-building-espresso-bar)r on Level 3 in the Natalie Bell Building
- The [Restaurant](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/restaurant) on Level 6 in the Natalie Bell Building
- The [Terrace Café](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/level-1-members-bar) on Level 1 in the Blavatnik Building

#### Tate Modern shops

There are opportunities to visit the shops at Tate Modern:

- The [River Shop](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/riverside-shop) on Level 1 in the Natalie Bell Building
- The [Terrace Shop](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/terrace-shop) on Level 1 in the Blavatnik Building
- The [Turbine Hall Shop](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/turbine-hall-shop) on Level 0 in the Natalie Bell Building

#### Member Facilities

The Members Bar is located on Level 5 Natalie Bell Building, accessible by lift from Level 4.

#### Multi-Faith and Contemplation Room

A multi-faith and contemplation room is available in the Natalie Bell Building on Level 4, off room 2 of the [Materials and Objects](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/display/materials-and-objects) display. This is a designated space for worship and prayer, as well as quiet and reflection. All are welcome to use this room.

#### Quiet Room

We have two quiet rooms available:

- A quiet room on Level 4 of the Natalie Bell Building can be accessed from Room 7 of [Materials and Objects](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/display/materials-and-objects)
- A quiet room on Level 2 of the Natalie Bell Building can be accessed from Room 4 of [Artist and Society](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/display/artist-and-society)

These rooms are for neurodiverse people, families or anyone who would like to spend some quiet time away from the gallery environment.

### Assistance dogs

We welcome guide dogs, hearing dogs and assistance dogs in the gallery. Drinking bowls are available at the Turbine Hall entrance – just ask a member of staff.

### Autism

To help plan your visit to Tate Modern, have a look at our [visual story](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/tate-modern-visual-story). It includes photographs and information of what you can expect from a visit to the gallery.

When you get to the gallery, ear defenders can be borrowed from the Ticket desks.

A quiet room is available to use in the Natalie Bell Building on Level 4, off room 7 of the [Materials and Objects](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern/display/materials-and-objects) display. This room is for neurodiverse people, families or anyone who would like to spend some quiet time away from the gallery environment.

Loud noises, flashing lights, smoke effects and strobe lighting feature in some artworks.

For more information before your visit contact us on:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call [+44 (0)20 7887 8888](tel:+44(0)2078878888) - option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)

_Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps_

### Blind and visually impaired visitors

#### Large print guides

Large print guides are available for all exhibitions.

You can access printed versions in the gallery:

- Ask a member of staff the exhibition entrance.

You can access PDF versions on our website:

- Visit the relevant exhibition page and click on the blue box 'Read the exhibition guide'; click on the 'Download large print guide' button near the top of the page to read the guide or to save a copy to your device.

Large print captions are currently not available for the permanent collection.

#### Magnifiers and Coloured Overlays

Magnifiers and coloured overlays are from all exhibition entrances. Please ask a member of the team for more information.

### Deaf and hard of hearing visitors

#### Hearing loops

The ticket desks are fitted with a hearing loop.

### Dyslexic visitors

- Coloured overlays and magnifiers are available. Ask a member of staff for more information.
- Large print captions are available in all exhibitions. Ask a member of staff at the exhibition entrance.

### Epilepsy and Seizures

Loud noises, flashing lights, smoke effects and strobe lighting feature in some artworks.

For more information before your visit contact us on:

- Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)
- Call [+44 (0)20 7887 8888](tel:+44(0)2078878888) - option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)

_Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps_ 

### Communication cards

Communication cards provide a means of visual, or nonverbal, communication.

You can use our communication cards to ask for directions to facilities in the gallery. These include toilet, café, seating, shop, quiet room, and exit. Show one of the cards to a member of Tate staff if you need to be shown to one of these places.

You can download these cards and print at home or save as a PDF on your portable device. There are two colour versions, with white or yellow background. Use whichever version you find easiest to read.

- [Print at home communication cards (white) 36.22 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1716/communication_cards_white_print.pdf)
- [Print at home communication cards (yellow) 35.96 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1717/communication_cards_yellow_print.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (white) 36.65 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1718/communication_cards_white_digital_1.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (yellow) 39.41 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1719/communication_cards_yellow_digital.pdf)

_Tate is grateful to Anna Farley who initiated and championed the development of these communication cards. Anna is an autistic artist who makes work exploring her autism, UK disability culture and inclusion._

### Access events

- [Touch Tours](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-modern/touch-tours) of the Tate Modern collection can be booked for free by calling 020 7887 8888 (10.00–17.00 daily)
- BSL interpretation, captioning and audio descriptions are offered at events where possible

[View all upcoming access events at Tate Modern](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?daterange=fromnow&event_type=access&gallery_group=tate-modern)

### Website

You can find the [accessibility statement for our website here](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/accessibility-statement).

### Contact Us

For queries about:

- mobility scooter reservations
- wheelchair reservations
- accessible car park reservations
- membership and ticketing services

Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)

Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 – option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00)

For queries about:

- general information to plan your visit

Email [ticketing@tate.org.uk](mailto:ticketing@tate.org.uk)

Call +44 (0)20 7887 8888 – option 1 (daily 10.00–17.00) 

Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition app

We want to make sure that all our galleries are welcoming and accessible, your feedback will helps us to continue improving.

If you would like to leave us a comment about your visit or your experience of our website you can send your thoughts to us in the email templates below:

- [Accessibility at Tate Britain](mailto:information@tate.org.uk?subject=%20Tate%20Gallery%20Access%20Contact%20Form%3A%20Access%20Feedback&body=Hello%0A%0AI%20want%20to%20give%20feedback%20about%20access%20at%20Tate.%0A%0AName%3A%0A%0AEmail%3A%0A%0AComment%3A)
- [Website feedback](mailto:information@tate.org.uk?subject=%20Tate%20Website%20Contact%20Form&body=Hello%2C%20%0A%0AI%20want%20to%20give%20feedback%20on%20a%20part%20of%20the%20website.%20%0A%0AName%3A%20%0AEmail%3A%0A%0APage%20or%20URL%3A%0A%0AComment%3A%20%0A%0A)

# Tate St Ives

Ticket or membership card required

Opening times

Tuesday to Sunday 10.00–16.20

Porthmeor Beach, St Ives, Cornwall TR26 1TG

Free for Members

- [Admission information](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#admission-information)
- [What's on](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#whats-on)
- [Plan your visit](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#plan-your-visit)
- [Getting here](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#getting-here)
- [In St Ives](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#in-st-ives)
- [Accessibility](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives#accessibility)

#### Uncover captivating stories of art on the Cornish Coast

Overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, Tate St Ives showcases work by artists including [Barbara Hepworth](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/dame-barbara-hepworth-1274), [Marlow Moss](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/marlow-moss-1671), [Naum Gabo](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/naum-gabo-1137) and [Patrick Heron](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/patrick-heron-1278), whose captivating works have brought international attention to St Ives and West Cornwall. Alongside displays from the Tate collection, the gallery presents modern and contemporary art from around the world through a dynamic exhibitions programme.

#### Book a ticket

From November 2026, we will be updating the Tate St Ives collection displays. Different galleries will be closed at different times while this takes place. The work will be completed in early 2027.

If you are coming to see a particular work of art, please [contact us](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/contact-us) before you visit.

[Book entry to Tate St Ives](https://shop.tate.org.uk/ticket/date?cgid=395702)

#### Barbara Hepworth Museum and Gardens

To visit the [Barbara Hepworth Museum](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/barbara-hepworth-museum-and-sculpture-garden) you will need an additional ticket.

[Book entry to the Barbara Hepworth Museum](https://shop.tate.org.uk/ticket/date?cgid=375790)

#### Free for Members

Members and Locals Pass holders enjoy unlimited free entry with no need to book, simply bring along your card.

[Become a Member today](https://shop.tate.org.uk/membership) [Get your Locals Pass](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/tate-st-ives-locals-pass)

## Admission information

### Entry details

The admission price includes [Wilhelmina Barns-Graham](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-st-ives/wilhelmina-barns-graham), [Modern Conversations](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/display/modern-conversations) displays (please note, rooms 1, 2 and 3 are closed), [Gözde İlkin: Those Who Remember Their Births](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-st-ives/g%C3%B6zde-ilkin-those-who-remember-their-births) and [Anna Farley: Your Space](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/display/anna-farley-your-space).

- £15.50 with donation, £14 without donation
- £14.50 with donation, £13 without donation for concessions

To visit the [Barbara Hepworth Museum](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/barbara-hepworth-museum-and-sculpture-garden) you will need an additional ticket.

#### More information

Tickets are limited and we encourage advanced booking. A limited number of tickets are available on the door.

- [Members](https://shop.tate.org.uk/membership) and [Locals Pass holders](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/tate-st-ives-locals-pass) enjoy unlimited free entry with no need to book, simply bring along your card
- Entry is free for visitors aged 18 and under

For more information see our [Booking and Ticketing FAQs](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/frequently-asked-questions/ticketing).

Group rates are available for groups of ten or more people when booked in advance. Find out more on our [Group visits](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/group-visits) page.

### Opening times

Tuesday to Sunday 10.00–16.20

Last entry 16.00

## Getting here

### Address

Tate St Ives 
Porthmeor Beach 
St Ives 
Cornwall TR26 1TG

### Directions

[Walk](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate St Ives,+Porthmeor Beach,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1TG,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e2) [Cycle](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate St Ives,+Porthmeor Beach,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1TG,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e1) [Ride](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate St Ives,+Porthmeor Beach,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1TG,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e3) [Drive](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate St Ives,+Porthmeor Beach,+St Ives,+Cornwall TR26 1TG,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e0)

#### ON FOOT

The gallery and museum are within walking distance of St Ives town centre and Porthmeor beach.

#### BY BICYCLE

There is a covered bicycle rack at the rear of Tate St Ives, by Barnoon car park. Property is left at the owner's risk. The entrance to Tate is a short walk down some steps towards Porthmeor Beach.

#### BY TRAIN

A frequent rail service operates between London Paddington and St Ives via Reading, Exeter, Plymouth, Bodmin, Truro, St Erth and Penzance. A local train service operates from St Erth to St Ives. For train times and booking see:

[National Rail Enquiries](http://www.nationalrail.co.uk/) or call 08457 000 125 [Great Western Railway](https://www.gwr.com/)

#### PARK & RIDE SERVICE

A park and ride service operates from St Erth train station, offering a scenic 10 minute journey into St Ives on the St Ives bay line. Visit [Great Scenic Railways for more information](https://greatscenicrailways.co.uk/stations/st-erth-park-and-ride/).

#### BY BUS

There are regular local bus services to and from St Ives.

[Traveline - local public transport information](https://www.traveline.info/)

#### BY COACH

There are daily National Express coach services from Victoria Coach Station, London. These services travel via Heathrow, Plymouth, Liskeard, St Austell, Truro, Redruth, Camborne, St Ives and Penzance – stopping at most small towns en route.

[National Express](http://www.nationalexpress.com/home.aspx)

#### SHUTTLE BUS SERVICE

A shuttle bus service operates during the peak spring and summer season (typically from March/May to September/October) between the [Trenwith Coach and Car Park](https://www.cornwall.gov.uk/transport-parking-and-streets/parking/cornwall-council-car-parks/trenwith-st-ives-tr26-1dd/) and St Ives town centre. From the town centre, Tate St Ives is approximately a 10-minute walk. For details of shuttle bus times and services, please contact St Ives Tourist Information on +44 (0)1736 796297.

#### BY CAR

St Ives is an historic fishing town with naturally narrow, largely car-free streets. While it’s only a 15–20 minute drive from the A30, driving can be stressful and parking is limited, so it's best to leave the car behind.

The St Erth Park and Ride is a popular option, letting you take in the scenic St Ives Bay train line, or you can park at Trenwith car park and taking the shuttle bus into town. If you plan to drive into St Ives, please plan ahead by visiting the [Cornwall Council website](https://www.cornwall.gov.uk/transport-parking-and-streets/parking/cornwall-council-car-parks/council-car-parks-in-st-ives-including-carbis-bay/).

Please note: Tate St Ives does not have a car park.

#### BY AIR

The nearest airport is in Newquay, the regional commercial airport for Cornwall.

[Newquay Airport](https://www.cornwallairportnewquay.com/)

### Accessible car parking

#### Tate St Ives

We have one parking bay in Barnoon car park for blue badge holders and people with mobility issues. The parking space is free with your gallery ticket. Please book your ticket and parking space at least 24 hours in advance.

To book call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+44(0)1736796226) 
Or email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk)

Once you have parked, you will enter via the Staff Entrance across the level terrace, approximately 10 metres from the parking space. From here, staff will facilitate your access to the gallery but may not be able to accompany you in the lift to the gallery level.

It is recommended to pre-book your gallery tickets before arrival either online or on the phone when reserving the parking space.

#### Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden

There is no parking space available at the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden.

### Wheelchair provision

Three wheelchairs are available to reserve for free. Bookings should be made at least 24 hours before visiting.

To book email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk) 
Or call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+44(0)1736796226)

Our passenger lift can accommodate wheelchairs with a width of no more than 80cm and a length of no more than 140cm. If you are using a chair of greater size please contact us and we can support an alternative route to our galleries.

### Entrances

#### Tate St Ives

There is one main entrance to the gallery. If you require a disabled car parking space, please see the Accessible car parking section of this page.

- There is a ramp into the main entrance from Porthmeor Beach.
- A flight of steps with a handrail
- From inside the building, there is lift access and level access to most areas of the gallery.

#### Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden

Wheelchair and buggy access to the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden is limited and requires assistance.

The lower floor of the museum is currently not accessible by wheelchair, however a handbook including photographs and detailed description of this space is available to support your visit.

Call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+44(0)1736796226) in advance to arrange your visit.

### Facilities at Tate St Ives

#### Information desk

The Information desk at Tate St Ives is located three metres away from the front of the building up an access ramp. Staff are happy to help with any questions you have about the artworks, building and facilities.

- There is level access to the Information desk from the main entrance.
- Lighting levels are generally bright but can be lower in some exhibition spaces, staff will be happy to advise.
- Seating is available in the circular entrance area, within the building and gallery spaces.

#### Toilets

A fully accessible [Changing Places](http://www.changing-places.org/) toilet is located close to Gallery 1. It has a height-adjustable changing bench and hoist. There is another accessible toilet close to Gallery 6.

#### Baby changing facilities

- The Parent and Baby Room is on the third floor between Gallery 3 and 4. It can accommodate a pushchair.
- There are also baby changing facilities in the main male and female toilets.

#### Lift

The lifts at Tate St Ives are suitable for wheelchair users. They give access to all floors at the gallery. If you are using a wheelchair with a width greater than 80cm please contact us and we can support an alternative route to our galleries.

#### Cloakroom

Coat hooks can be used for free or there are coin-operated lockers at our entrance. Bags and items larger than cabin bag size (55cm x 40cm x 20cm) are not permitted in the building.

#### Seating

There are seating places in the galleries and foyers. Folding stools and chairs are available for use at any time.

You’ll find the stools and chairs in different locations in the building and can ask a member of staff if you need one bringing to you.

### Assistance dogs

We welcome guide dogs, hearing dogs and assistance dogs in the gallery. Drinking bowls are available – just ask a member of staff.

### Autism

To help plan your visit to Tate St Ives, have a look at our [visual story](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-st-ives/tate-st-ives-visual-story). It includes photographs and information of what you can expect from a visit to the gallery.

When you get to the gallery, ear defenders can be borrowed from the information desk.

Loud noises, flashing lights, smoke effects, and strobe lighting feature in some artworks.

For more information before your visit contact us on:

- Email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk)
- Call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+44(0)1736796226)

_Our phone line supports the use of speech recognition apps_

### Blind and visually impaired visitors

#### Audio introduction

This 10 min introduction describes the architecture, layout and gives a brief taste of the exhibitions. 
With thanks to Art Fund and VocalEyes.

[Listen to the introduction here](https://soundcloud.com/vocaleyesad/tate-st-ives)

#### Audio Wall Text

To support visitors who prefer or require audio to engage with written information, the wall texts in our main exhibitions are also available in audio format. QR codes placed directly beneath each text panel allow visitors to scan and listen to a recorded reading on their own device.

#### Guide dogs

We welcome guide dogs, hearing dogs and assistance animals in the gallery. Drinking bowls are available – just ask a member of staff.

#### Talking Art

Talking Art sessions run throughout the year at Tate St Ives, designed for visitors who are blind or partially sighted and their friends. They provide detailed spoken descriptions of selected works on display in the changing exhibition, (often which can't be included in touch tours) alongside making activities.

#### Touch Tours

Available daily at Tate St Ives and the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden. 
Advance booking essential. An opportunity for blind or partially sighted visitors to touch selected sculptures from Tate Collection displays. Accompanied by a Touch Tour Guide, and wearing sculpture conservation gloves, participants are supported to touch and discuss the composition, materials, and histories of selected artworks on display in Modern Conversations at Tate St Ives, and at the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden.

To book a Touch Tour please contact us on:

- Email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk)
- Call [+44 (0)1736 791 177](tel:+44(0)1736791177)

### Deaf and hard of hearing visitors

#### Hearing loops

Hearing loops are fitted at the Information desks at Tate St Ives and the Barbara Hepworth Museum and Sculpture Garden. Hearing loops are also available on most talks and gallery tours.

#### BSL talks

BSL interpretation is offered where possible. [View upcoming access events at Tate St Ives.](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?daterange=fromnow&event_type=access&gallery_group=tate-st-ives)

### Concessionary admission

The concessions rate applies to students and disabled visitors (companion is free).

£5 tickets are available for recipients of Universal or Pension Credit.

Visitors aged 18 and under can enter the galleries for free with a ticket.

### Popular times

Whether you enjoy the lively atmosphere of our galleries or prefer a peaceful visit for leisurely viewing, we have a time that suits your preference.

**Peak Hours:** Tate St Ives is busiest daily between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM.

**Summer Trends:** During the summer, the busiest days are Tuesdays and Wednesdays, while weekends (Saturdays and Sundays) are generally quieter.

**Winter Trends:** In winter, this pattern reverses, with weekends becoming more popular.

For the best experience, we recommend checking our [What's On](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?gallery_group=tate-st-ives) page to see if any events are scheduled during your visit.

### Communication cards

Communication cards provide a means of visual, or nonverbal, communication.

You can use our communication cards to ask for directions to facilities in the gallery. These include toilet, café, seating, shop, quiet room, and exit. Show one of the cards to a member of Tate staff if you need to be shown to one of these places.

You can download these cards and print at home or save as a PDF on your portable device. There are two colour versions, with white or yellow background. Use whichever version you find easiest to read.

- [Print at home communication cards (white) 36.22 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1716/communication_cards_white_print.pdf)
- [Print at home communication cards (yellow) 35.96 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1717/communication_cards_yellow_print.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (white) 36.65 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1718/communication_cards_white_digital_1.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (yellow) 39.41 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1719/communication_cards_yellow_digital.pdf)

_Tate is grateful to Anna Farley who initiated and championed the development of these communication cards. Anna is an autistic artist who makes work exploring her autism, UK disability culture and inclusion._

### Website

Please find the accessibility statement for our website [here](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/accessibility-statement)

### Contact us

For:

- general information to plan your visit
- wheelchair reservations
- accessible car park reservations
- membership and ticketing services

Email [visiting.stives@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.stives@tate.org.uk) 
Call [+44 (0)1736 796 226](tel:+44(0)1736796226)

Please leave us a comment about your visit or your experience of our website. We want to make sure that all our galleries are welcoming and accessible, your feedback will help us to improve 
this.

[Visitor Feedback Form](mailto:information@tate.org.uk?subject=%20Tate%20Website%20Contact%20Form:%20Visitor%20Feedback&body=Hello%2C%20%0A%0AI%20want%20to%20give%20feedback%20on%20a%20visit%20to%20the%20gallery.%20%0A%0AName%3A%20%0AEmail%3A%0A%0APage%20or%20URL%3A%0A%0AComment%3A%20%0A%0A)

# Tate Liverpool + RIBA North

Free admission

Gallery 2 will be closed 2-26 November while we change the displays. The building will also be closed on 17 November for staff training and will close at 16.50 on 17 December.

Opening times

Monday to Sunday 10.00–17.50

Mann Island, Liverpool L3 1BP

© Tate (Brian Roberts)

- [What's on](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#whats-on)
- [Getting Here](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#getting-here)
- [Admission information](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#admission-information)
- [Visiting tips](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#visiting-tips)
- [Accessibility](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#accessibility)

© Tate (Brian Roberts)

## Welcome to Tate Liverpool + RIBA North

While our home on the Royal Albert Dock is being redeveloped, we have been temporarily based at RIBA North, Mann Island.

There are no further Tate exhibitions planned for our temporary space but visitors can explore two small displays curated by RIBA.

Visitors can also enjoy a small area for families, a ground floor display detailing the exciting plans for our new building and a small display upstairs showcasing the history of Tate Liverpool.

Tate Liverpool will reopen at the Royal Albert Dock in 2027.

[Find out about our redevelopment here](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/projects/transforming-tate-liverpool).

## What's on

Left Right

[Exhibitions\\ \\ **Ugo Rondinone: Liverpool Mountain**\\ \\ This gravity-defying sculpture celebrates Liverpool 2018\\ \\ Tate Liverpool\\ \\ Ongoing\\ \\ FREE](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-liverpool/ugo-rondinone-liverpool-mountain)

[Activities and workshops\\ \\ **Mildred's Albert Dock Art Trail**\\ \\ Help Mildred the gallery cat find artworks around the Dock\\ \\ Tate Liverpool + RIBA North\\ \\ Available every day\\ \\ FREE](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-liverpool--riba-north/mildreds-albert-dock-art-trail)

[Exhibitions\\ \\ **'Just Come in': 30 years of Maggie's Centres**\\ \\ Explore photography capturing people's experience of arriving at Maggie's centres\\ \\ Tate Liverpool + RIBA North\\ \\ Until 29 Nov 2026\\ \\ FREE](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-liverpool--riba-north/just-come-in-30-years-of-maggies-centres)

[All displays and events at Tate Liverpool](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on?date_range=from_now&gallery_group=tate-liverpool)

## Tate Members

## Getting Here

### Address

Tate Liverpool + RIBA North 
Mann Island 
Liverpool L3 1BP

### Directions

[Walk](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate Liverpool + RIBA North,+Mann Island,+Liverpool L3 1BP,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e2) [Cycle](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate Liverpool + RIBA North,+Mann Island,+Liverpool L3 1BP,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e1) [Ride](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate Liverpool + RIBA North,+Mann Island,+Liverpool L3 1BP,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e3) [Drive](https://www.google.co.uk/maps/dir//Tate Liverpool + RIBA North,+Mann Island,+Liverpool L3 1BP,+United+Kingdom/data=!4m2!4m1!3e0)

#### ON FOOT

Approaching from the Strand, continue straight on Strand Street until you reach Mann Island. Turn left and you'll reach the Mann Island development, a complex of three black buildings that sit between the Strand, the Canning Dock and the Museum of Liverpool.

#### BY BIKE

Bike racks are located close to the gallery, opposite the entrance to the Museum of Liverpool, beside the Great Western Railway building.

#### BY BUS

Liverpool ONE Bus Station on Canning Street is the closest bus station, but some buses drop off at the Pier Head, right next door to the gallery. Check the [Merseytravel website](https://www.merseytravel.gov.uk/) for details of local bus services.

#### BY TRAIN

The nearest train station to Tate Liverpool is James Street station, Liverpool L27PQ, which is approximately 2 minutes away. Liverpool Lime Street station, Liverpool's mainline railway station, is approximately 20 minutes away. Moorfields station, served by the Northern and Wirral Lines, is approximately 5 minutes away. Check the [Merseyrail website](https://merseyrail.org/) for details of local rail services.

#### BY FERRY

Mersey Ferries from Seacombe and Woodside on the Wirral call at the Pier Head, which is approximately 2 minutes away. Check the [Mersey Ferries website](https://www.merseyferries.co.uk/) for details of ferry services.

#### BY CAR

To get to Tate Liverpool + RIBA North, follow the brown signs to the Waterfront. The following car park is near Tate Liverpool + RIBA North: 
[Q-Park Liverpool ONE](http://www.q-park.co.uk/parking/liverpool/q-park-liverpool-one), with 2,000 underground spaces: 35 Strand Street, Liverpool L1 8LT.

#### BY COACH

The nearest coach station is on North Street (Liverpool City Centre), served by National Express coaches. More [information for drivers](https://albertdock.com/).

#### BY SHOPMOBILITY

Visitors may also like to make use of Liverpool’s Shopmobility service, on the third floor of the Liverpool ONE shopping centre. Equipment must be booked in advance and there is a charge. More [information for drivers](https://www.liverpool-one.com/).

## Admission information

### Entry details

There is no need to book to visit Tate Liverpool + RIBA North. Our displays are free to visit.

#### Schools and group visits

We would like to remind visiting schools and groups that our temporary building at RIBA North, Mann Island is much smaller than our Royal Albert Dock home.

- Groups do not need to book to view free displays at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North
- The recommended size for a group visiting the gallery is 15. It is important to split your group and stagger entry accordingly
- We do not have a lunchroom or any provision to provide space to eat lunches
- We do not have a cloakroom, lockers or an area to leave bags
- We would recommend a visit to Tate Liverpool + RIBA North as part of a wider visit to Liverpool as opposed to the sole focus of your visit

#### Bag size policy

For reasons of safety and security the following are not permitted in the building:

- bags larger than cabin bag size (55cm x 40cm x 20cm)
- sports or recreational equipment (musical instruments)
- large wheelie bags or boxes
- foldable bicycles, large skateboards and child or adult scooters

#### Security

We take security very seriously and work closely with [Police Project Servator teams](https://www.met.police.uk/projectservator). You can read more about our approach to [safety and rules for the gallery](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-gallery-rules).

### We're closed on

Thursday 24 December 2026

Friday 25 December 2026

Saturday 26 December 2026

Gallery 2 will be closed 2-26 November while we change the displays. The building will also be closed on 17 November for staff training and will close at 16.50 on 17 December.

### Opening times

Monday to Sunday 10.00–17.50

## Visiting tips

[read\\ \\ **Tate Liverpool + RIBA North visual story**\\ \\ A step-by-step visual and written guide to help you plan your visit](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool/tate-liverpool-riba-north-visual-story)

[read\\ \\ **Visit Tate Liverpool + RIBA North with your family**\\ \\ Find out about what's on offer for families at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool/visit-tate-liverpool-family)

[read\\ \\ **A guide to slow looking**\\ \\ Be amazed by the discoveries you can make when you look for longer at art](https://www.tate.org.uk/art/guide-slow-looking)

[read\\ \\ **Visiting tips for social care professionals**\\ \\ Information and resources to help social care professionals plan a visit to Tate](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/visiting-tips-social-care-professionals)

## Accessibility

- [Accessible car parking and drop-off](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-accessible-car-parking-and-drop-off)
- [Entrances to Tate Liverpool + RIBA North](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-entrances-to-tate-liverpool)
- [Wheelchair provision](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-wheelchair-provision)
- [Assistance dogs](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-assistance-dogs)
- [Autism](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-autism)
- [Blind and visually impaired visitors](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-blind-and-visually-impaired-visitors)
- [Deaf and hard of hearing visitors](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-deaf-and-hard-of-hearing)
- [Dyslexic visitors](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-dyslexic-visitors)
- [Facilities at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-facilities-at-tate-liverpool)
- [Communication cards](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-communication-cards)
- [Website](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-website)
- [Contact us](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool#tabs__section-contact-us)

### Accessible car parking and drop-off

There are two dedicated Blue Badge parking spaces located on Brunswick Street, which is 5 minutes away from Tate Liverpool + RIBA North. See the [Liverpool City Council website](https://liverpool.gov.uk/parking-roads-and-travel/find-parking/on-street-parking-bays/) for details about Blue Badge parking.

A [Q-Park Liverpool ONE](http://www.q-park.co.uk/parking/liverpool/q-park-liverpool-one), with 2,000 underground spaces: 35 Strand Street, Liverpool L1 8LT.

### Entrances to Tate Liverpool + RIBA North

Tate Liverpool is temporarily located at RIBA North, Mann Island.

- There are no steep gradients on approaches to Tate Liverpool
- There is level access to the gallery
- The main doors are operated manually

### Wheelchair provision

Wheelchairs are available to borrow during your gallery visit.

### Assistance dogs

We welcome assistance dogs and support animals in the gallery. Drinking bowls are available – just ask a member of staff.

### Autism

To help plan your visit to Tate Liverpool, have a look at our [visual story](https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-liverpool/tate-liverpool-riba-north-visual-story). It includes photographs and information of what you can expect from a visit to the gallery.

- Ear defenders can be borrowed from the front desk
- We can provide a quiet space, please ask a member of staff

Email [visiting.liverpool@tate.org.uk](mailto:visiting.liverpool@tate.org.uk)

### Blind and visually impaired visitors

#### Large print

We provide a range of text in large including information panels, labels and leaflets.

- All artwork labels are available in large print - just ask a member of staff
- Magnifiers are available in our gallery spaces, as well as overlays in a variety of colours. Please ask a member of staff for help
- We are working on delivering access tours. [Details of these tours will be available here.](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on)

### Deaf and hard of hearing visitors

BSL interpretation and captioning are offered where possible.

We are working on delivering access tours. [Details of these tours will be available here.](https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on)

### Dyslexic visitors

- We can provide various colours of transparent overlays, which may benefit some visitors with dyslexia when reading black and white text captions and leaflets.
- All artwork labels are available in large print at the entrance to each exhibition or display.

Just ask a member of staff.

### Facilities at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North

#### Entrance

A member of staff will be in the entrance and happy to help with any questions you have about the artworks, building and facilities.

- There is level access into the building from the entrance
- Lighting levels are bright

#### Toilets

Unisex toilets are located behind gallery 2 on the first floor, which can be accessed via the stairs or lift. 
The lighting levels are bright.

#### Accessible toilet

There is an accessible toilet behind gallery 2 on the first floor at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North, which all visitors can use.

This toilet is unisex. A key is not required for this toilet.

The door to the accessible adapted toilet opens outwards and is locked by a locking handle. As you face the toilet pan there is lateral transfer space of one metre on the left.

The tap type is sensory activated. There is a functional emergency alarm. Wall mounted grab rails are on both sides of the toilet.

Other features are placed at the following heights above floor level:

- Toilet seat: 50 cm.
- Hand dryer: less than 100 cm.
- Toilet roll holder: less than100 cm.
- Sink: less than 74 cm.

The contrast between the walls and floor is good. Wall mounted and drop down rails are available.

#### Changing Places toilet

The closest [Changing Places](http://www.changing-places.org/) toilet​ is at the [Museum of Liverpool](https://www.liverpoolmuseums.org.uk/museum-of-liverpool), located on their ground floor. Information is available on the Museum of Liverpool website. There is also a Changing places toilet available at the [Merseyside Maritime Museum](http://www.liverpoolmuseums.org.uk/maritime/visit/floor-plan/index.aspx) and in Liverpool One, which is located in the [Liverpool One Information Centre](http://www.disabledgo.com/access-guide/liverpool-city-council/liverpool-one).

#### Baby care facilities

There is one toilet with baby changing facilities at Tate Liverpool + RIBA North, located behind gallery 2 on the first floor.

#### Floors

The ground and first floor are accessible to the public.

- There 23 steps between the ground floor and the first floor
- The steps are clearly marked
- The lighting level is bright

#### Lift

There is one lift located at the back of the ground floor.

The lifts is prioritised for people who are not able to use the stairs.

- The lift is approximately 16 metres from the entrance
- The dimensions of the lift are 90cm by 110cm
- There is a mirror in the lift to aid reversing out
- The lift has an audible announcer
- The external call buttons are at a low level at the side of the lift
- The lighting level in the lift is bright

#### Skateboards, scooters, and folding bike policy

Electric skateboards, scooters and folding bikes are not permitted in the building.

#### Seating

Portable folding stools are available on request – ask a member of staff or at the information desks.

### Communication cards

Communication cards provide a means of visual, or nonverbal, communication.

You can use our communication cards to ask for directions to facilities in the gallery. These include toilet, seating, shop, quiet room, and exit. Show one of the cards to a member of Tate staff if you need to be shown to one of these places.

You can download these cards and print at home or save as a PDF on your portable device. There are two colour versions, with white or yellow background. Use whichever version you find easiest to read.

- [Print at home communication cards (white) 36.22 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1716/communication_cards_white_print.pdf)
- [Print at home communication cards (yellow) 35.96 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1717/communication_cards_yellow_print.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (white) 36.65 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1718/communication_cards_white_digital_1.pdf)
- [Digital communication cards (yellow) 39.41 Kb](https://www.tate.org.uk/documents/1719/communication_cards_yellow_digital.pdf)

_Tate is grateful to Anna Farley who initiated and championed the development of these communication cards. Anna is an autistic artist who makes work exploring her autism, UK disability culture and inclusion._

### Website

Please read our [accessibility statement](https://www.tate.org.uk/about-us/accessibility-statement) for our website

### Contact us

Email visiting.liverpool@tate.org.uk

## Exhibitions & Displays

### David Bowie: On Tour

Now open – Bringing together around 100 highlights from the V&A’s David Bowie archive – many that have never been on public display before

## One site, two sculpture parks, two galleries and lots for you to discover.

From [Pablo Picasso](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/pablo-picasso) to [Everlyn Nicodemus](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/everlyn-nicodemus), [Tracey Emin](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/tracey-emin) to [Anne Redpath](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/anne-redpath), the two magnificent galleries that make up the Modern, show some of the greatest works of art produced over the last 120 years. Set in scenic grounds, not far from the Dean Village, and yet still only a 15-20 minute walk from the city centre, the galleries offer a haven from the hustle and bustle of Edinburgh. 

At Modern One you can enjoy contemporary and modern art and encounter outstanding works of art from the world class Surrealism collection for free. At Modern Two you can see a dynamic programme of changing exhibitions - including our major retrospective this summer, [Gwen John: Strange Beauties](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/exhibition/gwen-john-strange-beauties). There are also permanent installations by artists including [Eduardo Paolozzi](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/eduardo-paolozzi) and [Nathan Coley](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/artists/nathan-coley). The galleries are only a few minutes’ walk from each other so make the most of your day and make sure you visit both.

## Which gallery would you like to visit?

### Modern One

Enjoy world class, contemporary and modern art for free.

[Plan your visit to Modern One Modern One](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/modern-one)

### Modern Two

See a dynamic programme of changing exhibitions and permanent installations.

[Plan your visit to Modern Two Modern Two](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/modern-two)

## Getting here

The Modern is located 15 minutes’ walk from Princes Street. It includes two buildings, Modern One and Modern Two, set in a beautiful sculpture park.

Modern One can also be reached via the Water of Leith walkway.

## Families

Dive into an outstanding collection of modern and contemporary art and stomp around the sculpture garden. Explore, create and play with [free summer activities](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/summer-art).

[Find out more](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/families)

### Learning Space

Our drop-in picnic and play space can be found on Level 2 in Modern One. You can help yourself to art books, big blocks and plenty of materials to make your own masterpieces – or just take a moment to chill out and eat your snacks.

### Free family trails

Pick up a special trail for all ages and stages - they'll get your family exploring the galleries, inside and out!

[Walk, Talk, Make Sculpture Trail Free family trails](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/features/walk-talk-make-sculpture-trail)

[Art Stomps for the under 5s Free family trails](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/families/art-stomps-for-the-under-5s)

### Take part!

Join one of our free, monthly workshops. At the Modern, Under 5s can take part in sculpture-hunting, art-stomping and feel-good making - while our older children can explore their own creativity with Your Art World Saturday morning workshops.

[Family events at the Modern Take part!](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/whats-on?what%5Ball_events%5D=all_events&what%5B46326%5D=46326&what%5B46311%5D=46311&what%5B46316%5D=46316&what%5B46321%5D=46321&what%5B46331%5D=46331&what%5B46336%5D=46336&what%5B46341%5D=46341&where%5Bmodern%5D=modern&when=on_now&audience=46296)

### Sensory Walks

Take some time out to explore the grounds, find our six creative prompts, scattered around the sculptures, and listen to a few stories - inspired by sculptures at the Modern.

[Sensory Sculpture Stories Sensory Walks](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/features/sensory-sculpture-stories)

[Sensory Signposts Sensory Walks](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/features/sensory-trail)

### Cafés and shops

### Café Modern One

**Open daily, 10am-5pm (last orders 4.30pm)**

Popin and enjoy lunch in the Modern One cafe or the beautiful terrace and garden to the rear of the gallery if it's a sunny day. Offering seasonal tasty salads, deli filled sandwiches, hearty soups, delicious hot dishes and artisanal baking - all prepared from scratch on the premises.

### Paolozzi's Kitchen

**Open daily, 10am-5pm (last orders 4.30pm)**

Located inside Modern Two and set around Paolozzi’s vast _Vulcan_ sculpture, experience a unique backdrop to lunch or coffee and cake! Inspired by the renowned Scottish artist and sculptor, Eduardo Paolozzi, this exciting restaurant serves Italian classics made with seasonal and local Scottish ingredients.  Come to our counter and try the delicious cakes and freshly baked homemade scones, available all day, every day. 

### Modern One Shop

**Open daily, 10am-5pm**

+44 (0)131 624 6494

The Modern One shop stocks collection gifts, books, limited edition prints, stationery, fashion, jewellery, homeware and exclusive products featuring well-loved images of artworks from the collection and beyond.

[Shop online](https://shop.nationalgalleries.org)

### Modern Two Shop

**Open daily, 10am-5pm**

+44 (0)131624 6494

The shop at Modern Two features an exhibition-inspired collection celebrating the quiet brilliance of Gwen John, from beautifully reproduced prints to books. You can also find beautiful homeware, stationery and art- inspired books and gifts. Shop online for gifts and custom prints delivered straight to your home.

[Shop online](https://shop.nationalgalleries.org)

## Green Tourism Award

National Galleries of Scotland are holders of a Green Tourism Gold award. This is the highest level award and demonstrates that we are an organisation committed to being an environmentally responsible visitor attraction, which champion sustainable practises within their operations and promote green tourism.  The Galleries were scored on a number of categories covering everything from how our buildings are managed, biodiversity on our grounds to social and equality issues.

[More about the Green Tourism Award](https://www.green-tourism.com/pages/home#about)

[Sustainability at National Galleries of Scotland](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/about-us/sustainability)

## Research facilities

All visitors are welcome to use our research facilities, whether for pleasure or for academic study. Visits are free but must be pre-booked.

### Prints and Drawings Study Room at Modern Two

Housing the international and Scottish collections of historic, modern and contemporary works of art on paper, the Prints and Drawings Study Room gives access to over 35,000 works of graphic art not on permanent display.

[Find out more Prints and Drawings Study Room at Modern Two](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/research-facilities/prints-drawings-study-room-modern-two)

### Reading Room at Modern Two

Home to our library, archive and special collections, the Reading Room is an outstanding resource on the history and theory of art from 1300 to the present. Visitors can access over 100,000 library items, 6,000 artists’ and special books and 140+ archival holdings.

[Find out more Reading Room at Modern Two](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/research-facilities/reading-room-modern-two)

### Gabrielle Keiller Library

The Gabrielle Keiller Library was specially designed by the architect Terry Farrell to house two key collections of Dada and Surrealist books and papers acquired in the mid-1990s.

[Find out more Gabrielle Keiller Library](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/visit/research-facilities/gabrielle-keiller-library)

## Venue Hire

Two stylish neo-classical venues for smart evening events with extensive parkland and unique interior artworks. Perfect venues for stylish parties, drinks receptions or product launches.

[More info](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/venue-hire/modern)

## About us

The National Galleries of Scotland cares for, develops, researches and displays the national collection of Scottish and international art and, with a lively and innovative programme of activities, exhibitions, education and publications, aims to engage, inform and inspire the broadest possible public.

[Find out more](https://www.nationalgalleries.org/about-us)

## Welcome!

**Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum opened in 1901 and is a firm favourite with local people and visitors.**

**It has stunning architecture and a family friendly atmosphere.**

Explore our 22 galleries and discover everything from art to animals, Ancient Egypt to Charles Rennie Mackintosh and so much more. 

If you only have one day in Glasgow, Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is a must see!

Get more info to plan your visit below. See 'Facilities' for cafe opening times and the current menu. 

**\*Important update: Restoration works at Kelvingrove\*** 
As part of a Glasgow City Council-funded programme of investment, we’re pleased to confirm that after a period of investigative work, further conservation and repair works began in September 2025. 

This project includes: 
•    Vital repair of historic stonework, roofing and windows 
•    Conservation of decorative features, including plaster and timber elements 
•    Improvements to roof drainage and lighting 
•    Preservation of original materials and design in line with Conservation Architect and Heritage best practices

The restoration programme is expected to span a significant period, during which some areas will be temporarily scaffolded.

**Changes to parking**

To facilitate the works parking spaces on the west side of the building are closed (they have been since 18 August 2025), significantly limiting the availability of parking. All disabled bays will remain available. 

Currently, there are 58 parking spaces in the car park, 10 of which are for blue badge holders,  2 are for Electric Vehicle charging and there is 1 motorbike bay.

Access to the car park will be restricted to cars only. All other traffic should use alternative parking options. Note: coaches can still access the designated bays on the east side of the building.

Alternative parking is available at Bunhouse Road, next to the Kelvin Hall. This is likely to be very busy, so we recommend using public transport if possible. Find out more here: [Public transport options](https://www.glasgowlife.org.uk/museums/venues/kelvingrove-art-gallery-and-museum#plan 'Public transport options')

**Kelvingrove will remain open to visitors throughout the restoration process.**

We appreciate your patience and support as we continue to invest in safeguarding one of Glasgow’s best-loved buildings.

### Wheelchair access

Manual wheelchairs are available to borrow from reception at Kelvingrove Art Gallery. These are free to borrow on a first come, first served basis.

### Cafe or restaurant

**KG Café**

Our café is situated in the lower level of the museum with some tables positioned in the conservatory area overlooking the park.  The café is operated by table service and is licensed serving spirits, wines, and bottled beers as well as a range of soft drinks. The menu offers options for starters, mains, and desserts but also a range of handmade sandwiches for a lighter option.  Hot beverages are available as well as a range of home baking.  Dietary requirements are well catered for, including vegan, gluten and dairy free options. Where possible we work with local suppliers and capture seasonality within the menu.

**KG Coffee Shop**

The coffee shop situated in the main hall on the upper ground floor is a more casual option with counter service but offers a magnificent view of the main hall. The coffee shop offers a range of hot and cold drinks, sandwiches, light bites and home baking. Dietary requirements are catered for, including vegan, gluten and dairy free options. Where possible we work with local suppliers and capture seasonality within the menu. Seating can occasionally be limited due to daytime events taking place in the hall.

Walk-in's only - no pre-booking necessary. 

**Borrow Cup**

As part of our commitment to reducing our use of disposable drinks cups, the KG Coffee Shop is now participating in the Borrow Cup scheme. For a £1 deposit, customers are served their drinks in a reusable Borrow Cup, this cup can then be returned to the café or another participating venue where the £1 deposit will be returned. [Click here for more information.](https://hubbub.org.uk/borrow-cup)

### Cloakroom

There is a £2 charge - cash only. Due to limited capacity, we can only store coats and small items. No prams, buggies or bulky items can be accepted.

### Parking

**\*Please be aware** that parking spaces on the west side of the building are currently closed, significantly limiting the availability of parking. All disabled bays will remain available. 

Access to the museum car park is restricted to cars only. All other traffic should use alternative parking options. Coaches can still access the designated bays on the east side of the building.

Alternative parking is available at Bunhouse Road, next to the Kelvin Hall. This is likely to be very busy, so we recommend using public transport if possible. Get info in the 'Plan your visit' section under 'Public transport options'.

There are 58 parking spaces in the car park, 10 of which are for blue badge holders and 2 are for Electric Vehicle charging and there is 1 motorbike bay.

Payment can be made either by coins, no notes or cards, or by the [RingGo phone /app.](https://myringgo.co.uk 'RingGo phone /app')

For more information about the RingGo process, please visit the [RingGo Cashless Parking](https://www.glasgow.gov.uk/index.aspx?articleid=27191 'RingGo Cashless Parking') page on the Glasgow City Parking website.

There are designated parking spaces (10) for Blue Badge holders and parking is free with no time restriction, subject to display of a valid permit. The spaces do not have to be booked in advance. For car park enquiries please contact 0141 276 1830.

### Public transport options

Use [**Traveline Scotland**](https://travelinescotland.com/) to plan your visit via public transport.

**Train** - The closest train stations are Partick (PTK), Charing Cross (CHC) and Exhibition Centre (EXG). These stations are roughly 1 mile away from Kelvingrove.

The lines for these stations run through the Low-Level platforms, at Glasgow Central (GLC) for Partick and Exhibition Centre and Glasgow Queen Street (GLQ) for Partick and Charing Cross.

Glasgow Central and Glasgow Queen Street are roughly 1.5 to 2 miles away from Kelvingrove.

**Underground** - The closest Subway station is Kelvinhall, which is roughly ½ mile away.

**Bus** - The bus stops at the front of Kelvingrove, on Argyle Street, have regular services from both directions. Services include:

- [First Bus](https://www.firstbus.co.uk/greater-glasgow 'https://www.firstbus.co.uk/greater-glasgow')\- services **2, 3 & 77**
- [McGill’s](http://www.mcgillsbuses.co.uk/) - service **17**
- The [City Sightseeing](https://www.citysightseeingglasgow.co.uk/) buses

**Please note:** If you are coming into Glasgow by train and planning to use a [PlusBus](https://www.plusbus.info/glasgow) ticket, the 100 bus and the City Sightseeing buses are not covered.

**Bike Hire** \- The [Voi Cycle](https://www.glasgow.gov.uk/article/3938/Cycle-Hire-Scheme) hire scheme is also in operation around Glasgow, with locations to pick up and drop off around the city.

**Bike Parking -** Short stay cycle shelters are available near to the  museum next to Kelvin Hall. [See here for more information.](https://cyclehoop.my.site.com/RentalsCommunity/resultsmap?postalCode=G3%208AW)

**Accessibility** - In case it is of use to anyone in your party, the [AccessAble](https://www.accessable.co.uk/venues/kelvingrove-art-gallery-museum) website has some useful accessibility information.

**Translate our webpages**

It is easy to translate our webpages to a language of your choice. The Glasgow Life website uses an accessibility toolbar, ReachDeck, which can auto-translate any page into different languages.

Just click on 'Languages and accessibility' on the top right hand corner of any page to open ReachDeck. When the toolbar opens, select the fifth icon along to translate the page into a selected language – then choose your chosen language in the drop-down menu.

## Overview

Admission

Free Entry

Donations welcome

You can donate at the venue or online.

[Get your free welcome pack](https://www.glasgowlife.org.uk/museums/digital-welcome-pack/gallery-of-modern-art-goma)

Home to the city’s contemporary art collection, including works by Turner Prize winners and emerging artists. 

GoMA is located in the centre of Glasgow. It houses four galleries, a library and gallery shop selling a range inspired by the Collection. 

GoMA is a world class art museum and a place for people to gather, to learn and to share ideas. We display, borrow and collect artworks from around the world.

The museum's collection includes a wide range of contemporary artworks, including paintings, sculptures, installations, videos, and digital art. The collection focuses on artists from Scotland, the UK, and the international art scene. GoMA regularly rotates its exhibitions, featuring both established and emerging artists, which ensures that visitors can experience a diverse range of contemporary art forms and perspectives.

Apart from its permanent and temporary exhibitions, GoMA also hosts educational programmes, workshops, talks, and events to engage the local community and foster dialogue about contemporary art. The museum aims to create an inclusive and accessible space where people from all backgrounds can connect with and explore contemporary art.
